summary.intent: Autonomously run the full GSD post-execute-phase ship loop (verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, ship PR, resolve reviews, extract learnings) for phase 69 (FUSE/WinFsp Rust integration + grant-root awareness), plus a mid-flight worktree cleanup and branch switch.
summary.outcome: Phase 69 was verified, secured (109-threat register, 0 open), validated, and shipped as PR #594 with all standard CI green and all 9 review threads resolved. The user-added Desktop E2E hard gate caught a real cross-language bug (file_iv encoded hex on the Rust mount vs base64 on the TS SDK, breaking every cross-client decrypt), which was root-caused and fixed (934302dea); macOS and Linux legs went green, and a follow-up fix to migrate a legacy-model test helper (bump-ipns-sequence.ts) was underway to close out the last Windows conflict-detection failure when the transcript ends.

repo: NodeContent.file_iv must be base64-encoded everywhere — the Rust FUSE mount was emitting hex while the TS/web node/v3 read chain (packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts) expects base64, causing 'Decryption failed' on every cross-client content read.
The cross-language KAT vectors' sample file_iv (000102...0b) is valid as both hex and base64, so it never discriminated the encoding bug — a KAT hardening gap.
cargo-windows CI job only proves the Windows platform code compiles; it does not run winfsp at runtime, so a green cargo-windows does not guarantee the Desktop E2E Windows leg passes.

Desktop E2E (desktop-e2e.yml, full macOS/Windows/Linux matrix) is workflow_dispatch-gated and does NOT run automatically on PRs — it must be explicitly dispatched via `gh workflow run "Desktop E2E Tests" --ref <branch>` to be a real gate.

coderabbit CLI times out summarizing full diffs over ~125 files/24k lines; scoping with `--dir <path>` per top-level area avoids the timeout but hits per-scope rate limits on the free tier (~46 min wait).

pr-release-preview.js's commit parser regex captures the description as `.+` (tolerates parens) and skips merge commits — it only fails on the non-conventional `type NN-NN:` space-format subject, not on parens in the description.
This repo squash-merges PRs, so branch commit history never reaches release-please post-merge; only the PR title needs to be conventional/paren-free.
gh pr edit fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL); patch PR body via `gh api -X PATCH repos/.../pulls/<N> -F body=@file` instead.
github-actions[bot] pushes a `chore(release)` commit to the PR branch after PR creation and after a passing Release Preview — always `git fetch` + rebase before the next push or it's rejected.
Commit via the repo's commit helper can appear to hang/timeout due to 1Password SSH signing, but the commit often lands anyway — verify with `git log --oneline -1` rather than retrying blindly.
markdownlint excludes `.planning/` from CI but prettier still runs there.
zsh treats `$status` as a read-only special variable — using it as a custom var name in a poll script silently breaks the script.

code.finding: publish_file_node wrote NodeContent.file_iv as hex; fixed to base64 (matching TS contract) at the wire boundary.
iv_hex computed here and threaded into journaled placeholder NodeContent.file_iv; needed to align with the base64 fix so replay (replay.rs:1099) publishes consistently.

is_unresolved predicate duplicated the enclosing cid.is_empty() check, making it always true and the pending_content fallback (lines 587-599) unreachable — caused read-after-write EIO on locally-buffered files.
Derived Debug on InodeKind leaked key material via Zeroizing's forwarding Debug impl; replaced with a manual redacting Debug impl.

Own-resolve generation check in fetch_node_gated deliberately compares floor-vs-floor (not the fetched node's actual generation) — looks like a bypass but is safe-by-design because seq/CID pairs are IPNS-signature-bound (confirmed via adversarial verification, not a bug).

Test helper was missed by the 69-25 node/v3 migration and still used the legacy folder model (vaultKeyBlob.rootFolderKey, folder.metadata.children), crashing on undefined.length under node/v3 — required a full rewrite to node/v3 APIs (unsealNode, updateFolderMetadataAndPublish).

workflow: Adversarial verification agents (dedicated skeptics reading actual code) caught multiple CodeRabbit/Greptile false positives in crypto-critical paths, preventing dangerous 'fixes' (e.g. a write-generation-protection 'bug' that was actually handled one level up in fs.rs).

When a CodeRabbit/security-auditor subagent stalls mid-stream with no output, checking whether it wrote partial artifacts and then manually assembling the report from already-gathered evidence (register + prior verification) can be faster and safer than re-spawning a long-running agent.

Running heavy compute (cargo test suites, CodeRabbit reviews) as the orchestrator in the background while briefing/spawning verification subagents in parallel avoided both RAM contention and idle waiting.
A hard CI gate (Desktop E2E) that exercises the true cross-language read path is worth the ~30-45 min wall time — it caught a bug that 476 unit tests, KAT vectors, and standard PR CI all missed.
GitHub GraphQL thread reply/resolve mutations are flaky and can fail silently; wrapping them in retry logic and re-querying reviewThreads afterward is necessary to confirm 0 unresolved.

friction: Initial git switch failed because the target branch was already checked out in a separate worktree; required manual cleanliness verification before removing it.

gsd-verify-work's default skill is a conversational UAT flow, not the goal-backward automated verifier needed for an autonomous phase-Rust ship — had to detect no VERIFICATION.md existed and drive the verifier directly.

The security auditor subagent stalled mid-stream with an API error after ~7.5 minutes, producing no SECURITY.md — had to reconstruct the report manually from the threat register and existing verification evidence.
CodeRabbit CLI timed out summarizing the full 125-file diff; had to fall back to per-directory scoped reviews, one of which (apps/desktop) then got rate-limited on the free tier.
Commits appeared to time out/fail due to 1Password SSH signing hangs, requiring manual verification via git log to confirm they actually landed before proceeding.
A background poll script failed because it used `$status` as a variable name, which zsh treats as read-only.
gh api log retrieval for failed CI steps came back empty multiple times (logs still flushing), requiring repeated attempts to get the actual failure text.
Desktop E2E matrix runs take ~30-45 minutes each, and had to be dispatched/polled three separate times (initial red run, post-69-14 rebuild, post-file_iv-fix) before reaching a near-green state.
Linux desktop-e2e failed on an unrelated CI-infrastructure flake (postgres-setup action version pinning), confounding triage of the real product bug until isolated.
GraphQL review-thread reply/resolve mutations failed silently on first attempts and needed explicit error output and retries to succeed.
open_items: Grant-scope shared-scope-exit rotation is fail-closed (returns EIO) but not live-wired — no production RotationDeps implementor exists yet (ROT-07 live-wiring gap); tracked as a deferred todo, folded in the grant-scope gate correctness findings.
SDK floor-store non-atomic read-modify-write concurrency/atomicity issue (mirrors the shipped TS twin's identical behavior) — deferred as a todo rather than fixed under time/risk pressure.

FUSE publish/concurrency hardening items deferred: CAS-retry consolidation (5→2 attempts flagged as regression risk), journal_helpers key-hygiene Zeroizing promotion and dead clone removal, plus minor desktop hygiene notes.
Node-codec KAT blind spot: the sample file_iv value is valid under both hex and base64, masking the encoding bug — filed as a high-priority todo to pin a KAT sample that's only valid in one encoding.

Windows conflict-detection desktop-e2e leg was failing due to bump-ipns-sequence.ts's un-migrated legacy model; migration to node/v3 was completed and committed at the very end of the transcript but final Windows e2e confirmation had not yet run.
PR #594 left unmerged — the user reserved the final merge decision per the operating rules.
